doc.title: Marty Sheller interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 9, 2022

title: Joining Mongo's band and how 'Watermelon Man' reached Mongo
summary: Donald Byrd recommends Herbie Hancock, Mongo adopts 'Watermelon Man', horn phrasing and the passed-on 'Cantaloupe Island'.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Good statement. So you’ve been involved in a couple of really terrific recordings with Mongo and I wanted to ask a specific question about the “Watermelon Man” and you know I’ve read about how that sort of came about.
But the terrific thing that the horns did. Instead of playing [scats] they went [scats].
Well I have to take credit for that one.

I was the one. I don’t know whether you read the story Herbie Hancock has told how it got to Mongo. Herbie had recorded “Watermelon Man” I think around the summer of ’92. And somewhere down the line Mongo was doing — oh I remember — Mongo was playing a gig in a little club in the Bronx and Chick Corea was the pianist but Chick had already given notice a long time ago that he wasn’t going to be available for that gig and Mongo was at Symphony Sid’s office and Donald Byrd was there. And when Donald Byrd heard that Mongo needed a piano player for Friday, Saturday and Sunday, he said that, “If you’re hung up for a piano player, I know a piano player, a great piano player. He reads really well. I doubt whether he’s ever played in a Latin band but if you need somebody to sit behind a keyboard and play there’s a guy available. His name is Herbie

Hancock.” So Herbie played that gig Friday, Saturday and Sunday, and Donald Byrd came to the gig one of those nights and Donald, Herbie Hancock and Mongo were talking about the influence of Latin and Cuban music on funk music. And Donald Byrd said to Herbie Hancock, “Play that little vamp ‘Watermelon Man.’” So Herbie played “Watermelon Man” and Mongo really liked it, told him to come by rehearsal, new rehearsals starting on Monday, which is the first rehearsal that I made with the band. And we played “Watermelon Man.” We rehearsed it that week and did a gig on the weekend at a club in Brooklyn and played “Watermelon Man,” the people were going crazy. And when it came to playing the melody I thought of somehow, a guy who was going to sing, “hey watermelon man” is not going to be going [scats] he’s going to be a [scats]. So he started phrasing it that way. And matter of fact an interesting story, after it became a hit Mongo asked Herbie if he had another song similar to that, something, another funk kind of a song. So Herbie said yeah, and he brought by a song called “Cantaloupe Island.” And we rehearsed it a couple of times and then Herbie left the rehearsal and Mongo said, “Naaa. I think I’ll pass on this one.” Little did he know — so we never got to record that.
If we did we would have been the first ones to have recorded it.
Yeah lightning didn’t strike twice for Mongo on that one.
